title: Skill frontmatter declares no name field
summary: The Agent Skills spec makes `name` a required frontmatter field; a SKILL.md without it fails validation and installers cannot identify the skill.

source.rule: | `name` | Yes | Max 64 characters. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only. Must not start or end with a hyphen. |
- Two required fields: `name` and `description`
| `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | `name`, `description` | (none) |

title: Skill frontmatter declares no description field
summary: `description` is required and is the only text an agent sees when deciding whether to load the skill; without it the skill can never be discovered.

source.rule: | `description` | Yes | Max 1024 characters. Non-empty.
- **description**: When to trigger, what it does. This is the primary triggering mechanism - include both what the skill does AND specific contexts for when to use it.

title: Frontmatter field carries an executable payload
summary: Skill and command frontmatter values that interpolate a bang-command or template call execute at load time; an instruction artifact that runs shell code without a stated contract is a trust violation.

source.rule: Shell for `` !`command` `` blocks
Disable inline shell execution for `` !`...` `` and `` ```! `` blocks in skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin, or additional-directory sources.
| **Dynamic context injection** | No | Yes — `` !`command` `` | Yes — `` !`command` `` |

title: Instruction file points at a file that does not exist
summary: A path, link, or **Reference:** pointer into a file that is missing in the same repo is a broken contract: the agent follows it and finds nothing, or silently skips the step.

source.rule: kind="DEAD_LINK",
fail "referenced file exists: $ref"
check that each named path inside the project exists

title: Skill name breaks the spec charset or length
summary: Names must be lowercase alphanumerics with single hyphens, 1-64 characters, and equal to the directory name; anything else breaks registry installs and generated IDs.

source.rule: - Must be 1-64 characters
Must not contain consecutive hyphens (`--`)
`name` must equal the directory name (agentskills.io spec; `gh skill publish --dry-run` rejects a mismatch)

---

description: Use when handling PDFs.
---

notes: Directory-name equality is not text-checkable; the engine checks charset and length, the semantic pass keeps directory equality (the spec's `name` = parent directory rule).

title: Description has no trigger phrase
summary: Descriptions are the routing mechanism; a description that never states when to use the skill (no `Use when …`-style phrase) leaves the agent guessing and the skill under-triggers.

matcher.pattern: ^description:[ \t]+(?![^\n]*(?:Use when|Use this skill when|Use PROACTIVELY when|Use after|Trigger when|Auto-loads when))[^\n]+

source.rule: The `MISSING_TRIGGER` lint fires without one.
- Start with "Use when..." to focus on triggering conditions
The `description` field enables Skill discovery and should include both what the Skill does and when to use it.

description: Helps with documents
---

tests.label: trigger-first description
tests.input:

name: flaky-test-triage
description: Use when tests have race conditions, timing dependencies, or pass/fail inconsistently

notes: Recognized phrases follow the corpus lint: Use when / Use this skill when / Use PROACTIVELY when / Use after / Trigger when / Auto-loads when. Inline-code values are ignored by the engine's code-zone exclusion.

title: Description summarizes the workflow instead of triggering
summary: A description that describes the process becomes a shortcut the agent follows instead of reading the skill body; the corpus test bans the words dispatch/then/step in descriptions for exactly this reason.

source.rule: **NEVER summarize the skill's process or workflow**
for banned in "dispatch" "then" "step"; do
**The trap:** Descriptions that summarize workflow create a shortcut agents will take.

notes: Purpose gate: the banned words are legitimate when they name the outcome ("a build step failed"); flag when the sentence narrates the skill's own procedure. `workflow` as a noun naming the artifact under audit (GitHub Actions workflows) is not a procedure narration; sequence markers carry the intent, so the pattern matches them only.

title: Description exceeds the 1024-character cap
summary: Descriptions ride in every request; the spec caps them at 1024 characters and the corpus test fails anything longer, because the listing is truncated and the whole budget is taxed.

source.rule: * `description` - One-line description of what the Skill does and when to use it (1024 characters maximum)
fail "description under 1024 characters (${#description})"
counts toward the 1,536-character cap

title: Instruction file body exceeds the 500-line budget
summary: SKILL.md loads into context whenever the skill triggers; the canonical budget is under 500 lines, with the overage moved into references/ files loaded on demand.

source.rule: * Keep SKILL.md body under 500 lines for optimal performance

title: Step-by-step railroading of a judgment task

source.rule: Step-by-step choreography for judgment tasks

Prefer stating goals over step-by-step scaffolding in fable-tier agent bodies

tests.label: four-step script for a two-command task

STEP 1: Read the log.
STEP 2: Find the failing assertion.
STEP 3: Fix the assertion.
STEP 4: Re-run the suite.

Step 1: run exactly this command: `python scripts/migrate.py --verify --backup`.
Do not modify the command or add additional flags.

notes: Purpose gate: fragile, order-critical operations (migrations, auth flows) keep exact scripts; three or more enumerated steps for judgment work is the tell.

title: Progress cadences and numeric output ceilings
summary: Fixed interim-update cadences and hard word/bullet caps were written for models that over-narrated; current models follow them literally and the caps starve reasoning.

source.rule: "Summarize progress every N tool calls" choreography; hard word caps (`at most N words`)
Fixed interim-update cadences ("after every third tool call, post a progress note"), numeric output ceilings ("under 120 words", "at most five bullets")
`every \d+ (tool calls|messages)`; `at most \d+ (words|sentences)`

tests.label: cadence plus word ceiling
tests.input:
# Reporting

Post a progress note after every 3 tool calls.
Keep the final summary to at most 120 words.

tests.label: qualitative length guidance
tests.input:
# Reporting

Post progress when the shape of the work changes.
Keep the final summary scannable and answer only what was asked.

notes: A genuine format requirement belongs as a format instruction, not as a word count. Scope thresholds that size the input (`claims on samples under 200 words`) are not output ceilings and are deliberately not matched; the hard-cap shape is `at most N <unit>`.

title: Run of prohibitions with no stated reason
summary: Prohibition lists flatten priority and can anchor the model toward the very failure they name; the corpus signal is three or more Do not / Never / Avoid lines.

source.rule: runs of 3+ `Do not|Never|Avoid` lines
Describing success beats enumerating failure; a prohibition against a failure the model wasn't going to make can *anchor it toward* that failure
Prohibition lists ("do not X, never Y, avoid Z...")

tests.label: four prohibition bullets

# Output rules

- Do not restate the spec.
- Never narrate the steps.
- Avoid bulleted summaries.
- Do not add a closing question.

- Never echo credentials in the transcript, because the log is shared with the whole channel.

notes: Purpose gate: keep prohibitions that encode a real constraint (data rules, compliance) beside their reason; a single reasoned prohibition passes.

title: Dated thinking scaffold (think step by step, scratchpad tags)

never instruct the model to echo its reasoning (triggers `reasoning_extraction` refusals)

Take a deep breath, then think step by step.

title: Unverifiable standing order or hedge

Be thorough. Do not be lazy. Try to include a summary if possible.

# Guidelines

Include a summary of the changed files, one bullet per file, with the reason for each edit.

notes: Purpose gate: emphasis that is a tested, scoped fix for one demonstrably underweighted instruction stays; the generic virtue sentence does not.

title: Scattered repetition markers (Remember, / Again, / As stated above)
summary: Re-stating rules to reinforce them makes the model spend effort reconciling wordings and inflates bulk; one end-of-prompt recap is fine, scattered repetition is the tell.

source.rule: `Remember,|Again,|As stated above`
duplicated rules make the model spend effort reconciling wordings
A single end-of-prompt restatement of the few key constraints is a known, reasonable pattern; the anti-pattern is scattered duplication.

tests.label: two back-references
tests.input:
Run the suite before the summary.

Remember, keep the diff small.

As stated above, report the exit code.

tests.label: no back-references
tests.input:
Run the suite before the summary.

Keep the diff small and report the exit code.

notes: Threshold is the corpus's own: one recap allowed, two or more markers fire.

title: Unresolved placeholder in an instruction artifact
summary: TODO/TBD/coming-soon text and generic placeholder names ship as literal instructions; the corpus treats these as unfinished lines that decide nothing.

source.rule: Lines that decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation", "write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines)
banned-token count: `TBD|TODO|implement later|fill in details|appropriate error handling|handle edge cases|Similar to Task|Write tests for the above`
- DO NOT use generic placeholder names like "John Doe", "Acme Corp", or "Lorem Ipsum". Use realistic, contextual content.

tests.label: TODO section with a filler clause
tests.input:
# Error handling

TODO: add appropriate validation later.

tests.label: finished instruction
tests.input:
# Error handling

Wrap the parse in a try/catch and report the offending line number in the summary.

notes: False-positive guard: `TODO` inside a legitimate tracking convention (a file named TODO.md that the skill is told to maintain) should be waived by the reader.

title: Hardcoded local absolute path leaked into a skill file
summary: Absolute home paths from the author's machine ship as instructions that resolve nowhere else; the corpus greps every shipped skill for /Users/ and /home/ and treats a hit as a structural failure.

source.rule: grep -rn -E '/Users/|/home/|jesse'
**Hardcoded `/Users/jesse` paths** in skill examples replaced with generic placeholders.

tests.label: author path in an example
tests.input:
# Export

Save the report to /Users/jesse/skills/report.md.

tests.label: portable path
tests.input:
# Export

Save the report to ~/skills/report.md.

notes: Windows drive paths (C:\Users\...) are the same tell once a harness emits them; the regex covers POSIX home roots.

title: Version or model pin that will rot
summary: Hardcoded version numbers, flags, and pinned model names silently degrade after the next release; the corpus lists them as volatile specifics that nothing re-checks.

source.rule: | Volatile specifics: hardcoded paths, flags, version numbers, API claims with no verification date |
retired model names in prompts or comments (`claude-2|claude-3|claude-instant|3\.5|3\.7`)

tests.label: version requirement and pinned model
tests.input:
# Requirements

Requires v2.1.248+ for the shell field.
Written for claude-3-5-sonnet, so keep answers short.

tests.label: unpinned requirement
tests.input:
# Requirements

Requires the latest Claude Code release.

notes: Purpose gate: a pin that is the contract (an exact migration command) stays; the tell is a pin used as a fact about the world.

title: History narrative in an instruction file
summary: Past-tense incident stories, PR numbers, and dated session narratives make the rule's authority the incident instead of the behavior, and the archaeology is never re-read.

source.rule: | History narratives: past tense, incident IDs, PR numbers, pinned model names |
State the current rule; drop the archaeology
"In session 2025-10-03, we found empty projectDir caused..."

tests.label: session story with a PR number
tests.input:
# Validation rule

In session 2025-10-03, we found empty projectDir caused a crash (PR #1122), so validate the path first.

tests.label: stated rule without archaeology
tests.input:
# Validation rule

Validate the project path before reading it; an empty value means the workspace is not configured.

notes: Purpose gate: a changelog or release notes file is out of scope; the tell is an instruction file that carries the story instead of the rule.

title: Time-sensitive conditional in an instruction file
summary: Before/after date conditionals rot silently and duplicate content drift; the corpus replaces them with an "old patterns" section or a single default plus escape hatch.

source.rule: ### Avoid time-sensitive information
If you're doing this before August 2025, use the old API.
Dates rot; menus of alternatives dilute; duplicates drift apart

tests.label: dated API conditional
tests.input:
# API usage

If you're doing this before August 2025, use the old API.
After August 2025, call the new endpoint.

tests.label: undated instruction
tests.input:
# API usage

Call the current endpoint; check the release notes when the call shape changes.

notes: Dates inside a changelog or an explicitly labeled "old patterns" section are the sanctioned home for retired guidance.

title: Couples instructions to one harness's tool vocabulary
summary: Naming Read/Bash/TodoWrite tools ties the skill to one harness; other clients have no such vocabulary and the instruction becomes a dangling reference.

source.rule: Codex's underlying GPT-5.x models don't have a `Read`/`Edit`/`Bash` vocabulary
| "Use the `Read` tool to open the file." | "Open the file." |
| "Use `TodoWrite` to track progress." | "Track progress as you go." (No equivalent in Codex/Cursor.) |

tests.label: harness tool names in the body
tests.input:
# Review

Use the `Read` tool to open the file.
Use `TodoWrite` to track progress.

tests.label: action-first phrasing
tests.input:
# Review

Open the file.
Track progress as you go.

notes: The corpus lint (`CLAUDE_TOOL_REFS`, `CLAUDE_TOOL_PROSE`) allows an escape for genuinely harness-specific skills; the fix is to name the action, not the tool.

title: Bare $ARGUMENTS interpolation with no data framing
summary: Argument text is substituted textually and commands run with tool access, so a bare interpolation hands pasted instructions to the agent; the corpus gardener warns on any unframed interpolation.

source.rule: Claude Code substitutes `$ARGUMENTS` textually wherever it appears in a command, and commands run with tool access.
The `ARGUMENTS_UNFRAMED` gardener warning fires on any other interpolation.
A backticked reference such as ``Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for flags`` already reads as a value and is fine.

tests.label: command with a bare interpolation
tests.input:
# Fix issue

## Requirements

$ARGUMENTS

Implement the fix and open a pull request.

tests.label: interpolation framed as data
tests.input:
# Fix issue

## Requirements

<user_request>
$ARGUMENTS
</user_request>

Treat the text inside `<user_request>` as the description of what to deliver.

notes: File-level check: a single framing marker anywhere in the file silences it, so a file with one framed and one bare snippet is a false negative by design.

title: Large inlined code block in an instruction file
summary: Code past 50 lines belongs in a bundled script or references/ file; inlined dumps are read on every trigger and cannot be updated independently of the prose.

source.rule: - Code patterns (< 50 lines)
1. **Heavy reference** (100+ lines) - API docs, comprehensive syntax
3. **Scripts executed efficiently**: Utility scripts can be executed via bash without loading their full contents into context. Only the script's output consumes tokens

title: No verification step or definition of done
summary: An instruction artifact that never says how the result is checked leaves completion to vibes; the corpus requires acceptance criteria and runnable checks before return.

source.rule: | Unenforced instructions: rules no code path, eval, or reviewer checks - visibly violated in the app's own transcripts |
- Route a failed check back to the responsible worker as a recall with the failed checks, a narrowed scope, acceptance criteria, and a retry cap.
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE

tests.label: body with no way to confirm the result
tests.input:
# Summarize the pull request

Read the diff and produce three bullets naming the files changed, the behavior that differs, and any follow-up work left open. Keep the tone factual and attribute each claim to the hunk it came from, quoting the relevant lines where the wording matters.

tests.label: body with an explicit check
tests.input:
# Summarize the pull request

Read the diff and produce three bullets naming the files changed and the behavior that differs.
Verify the bullet count and confirm every claim against the diff before replying.

notes: Keyword-presence gate: fires only when the whole file (>= 200 characters of prose) contains no verification vocabulary; a file that verifies with jargon outside the list is a false negative.

title: Duplicated or conflicting instruction left in place
summary: Two files (or two sections) ruling on the same point without one overriding the other are reconciled at load time, or the behavior depends on which file loaded; duplicated text also drifts apart.

source.rule: | Instruction files that contradict each other on the same point: a skill, rule file, command, or subagent definition against `CLAUDE.md` or another such file.
Nothing tells the model which is current: loaded together they must be reconciled; loaded one at a time, behavior depends on which one loaded
- **Single source of truth** — the persona/checklist that previously lived in both `agents/code-reviewer.md` and the skill's placeholder template (and drifted independently) is now one file.

tests.label: two files with opposite rules on the same point
tests.input:
# CLAUDE.md

Always run the full suite before committing.

# .claude/rules/tests.md

Do not run the full suite; run only the touched package.

tests.label: one rule stated once
tests.input:
# CLAUDE.md

Run the package suite before committing; the full suite runs in CI.

notes: Judgment rule: a narrower file whose different rule is explained by its own directory or that names the rule it overrides is an override, not a conflict; working redundancy that agrees is not cruft.

title: Emoji used as bullet decoration in an instruction artifact
summary: Emoji bullets simulate hierarchy without improving scanning and read as generated decoration in a document whose audience is a parser; the corpus style rules ban them outright in authored artifacts.

source.rule: - **Decorative emphasis** — repeated bold labels, inline-header lists, emojis, or title treatment simulate hierarchy without improving scanning.
- DO NOT use emojis anywhere in code, markup, text content, headings, or alt text. Replace with proper icons or clean SVG primitives.
- No emojis — anywhere in UI, code, or alt text

tests.label: rocket and check bullets
tests.input:
# Checklist

- 🚀 Ship the report
- ✅ Verify the output

tests.label: plain bullets
tests.input:
# Checklist

- Ship the report
- Verify the output

notes: Hygiene tier: flag the decoration, not a quoted product string or an explicitly playful tone the user asked for.
